prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 56-72 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a crouching grey stone gargoyle on two clawed feet, cracked stone skin with chipped edges, two bat wings of stone half raised behind the shoulders, two short curved horns, a snarling face with a wide fanged mouth and glowing orange eyes, long arms with clawed hands, a short pointed tail; in every cell the whole figure is centred in its own cell with empty space on both sides, and its reaching claws and wings stop well before the edges of its cell. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: its snarling stone face with glowing orange eyes and fangs is readable.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, springing forward at the heroes with both clawed hands raking down in front of its chest, the elbows bent so the claws stay well inside the middle cell, the two wings raised up behind it (exactly two wings, as in the idle cell), facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, both wings still visible behind the shoulders and half folded (exactly two wings, as in the idle cell), cracks across its chest, the arms thrown up, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. The two stone bat wings stay attached behind the shoulders in every cell and spread or fold with the motion (exactly two wings, as in the idle cell). Use a strong diagonal line of action through the whole body, shift the weight clearly onto one leg, twist the torso and extend the arms and claws far from the body. Draw only the parts and clothing named in the description, the same in every cell: no cape, cloak, scarf or extra cloth, and no slash trail, smear, motion arc or motion lines. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, standing on two feet, both feet on the ground line. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, red skin, a trident, a pedestal, feathers, a weapon, a third wing, a cape, flying stone chips.
